issues.description: FAQ example reads req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) but the invariant is muddled and the test asserts 400 for a case that cannot occur.
issues.detail: If content_length is 1 and body is empty, the client/transport will not deliver a body of length 1; reading 1 byte will either block or return fewer bytes. The example's invariant — 'header says N bytes, stream yields M, with M<N implies 400' — is not stated. Without it the reader cannot tell whether this tests a real condition or an artifact of the test client.

issues.description: The change from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() in the example is unexplained and alters termination semantics.
issues.detail: stream.read() reads to EOF; bounded_stream.read() reads exactly Content-Length bytes (and blocks/short-reads if the body is shorter). This is precisely the behavior the new negative test exercises, yet no comment in things_advanced.py states the invariant or why the switch was made. A reader cannot reconstruct the reasoning without diffing history.

issues.description: README diff contains unrelated cosmetic and semantic changes beyond the PR's stated scope.
issues.detail: The reordering of imports, removal of blank lines after class headers, reformatting of HTTPUnauthorized calls, and notably the signature change of StorageError.handle from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params) are not described in the PR summary. The argument-order change is a real semantic shift (Falcon error handler signature) and deserves its own commit and rationale, not a silent ride-along.

issues.description: Test assertions use parenthesized form assert(result.status == ...) which reads as a function call, not an assert.
issues.detail: assert is a statement; assert(expr) is equivalent to assert expr but visually misleads readers into thinking assert is a function. In a literate example shown in the FAQ this matters more than in private test code — readers copy the style. Prefer assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400.

issues.description: New tests lack any comment stating what invariant each request exercises.
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 are added without a single line explaining 'resp3: well-formed POST returns 201' and 'resp4: Content-Length=1 with empty body returns 400 because bounded_stream.read yields no bytes'. The tests are correct but opaque; a future reader hitting a regression must reverse-engineer intent from status codes.

issues.description: FAQ PostTest example mixes None and 0 in a way that hides a branch.
issues.detail: The outer check 'if req.content_length in (None, 0)' already excludes both, yet the inner read uses 'req.content_length or 0' as a defensive fallback that can never trigger in this branch. Either the guard is redundant or the inner expression is — pick one. Dead defensive code teaches readers the wrong lesson.

review.summary: The PR adds two useful POST tests for things_advanced and an FAQ entry on header customization, but it carries an unstated semantic change (stream.read → bounded_stream.read) that is the actual reason the negative test passes — and that invariant is never written down. The README diff sneaks in unrelated reformatting plus a real signature change to StorageError.handle, which should not ride along silently. The FAQ example is correct enough but pedagogically muddled: redundant guards, parenthesized asserts, and an unstated invariant about what Content-Length=1 with an empty body actually means at the transport layer. UNDER-AUDITED overall: the behavior is plausibly right, but the explanation a careful reader needs is missing.
